description: Batch strict predecessor and successor queries using an x-fast separator trie over sorted small clusters.

source.title: Log-logarithmic worst-case range queries are possible in space Theta(N)
source.author: Dan E. Willard
source.copyright: Algorithm idea and citation only; implementation and contract are clean-room work.

output.meaning: sum((one_based_query_index)*((strict_predecessor+1)+65537*(strict_successor+1))); a missing neighbor is -1 and contributes zero

algorithm_details.primary: Sort keys into consecutive clusters of at most 16; build a 16-bit binary trie over cluster maxima, storing each subtree's minimum cluster rank. Walk the trie to select the first cluster maximum at least the query, then binary-search the cluster for strict neighbors and cross an adjacent cluster boundary if necessary.
algorithm_details.independent_oracle: Sort keys and use lower-bound and upper-bound positions to find the strict predecessor and successor.
algorithm_details.primary_complexity: The language ports use insertion sort, giving O(N^2 + 16 ceil(N/16)) preprocessing time and O(N + 16 ceil(N/16)) space; queries cost O(16+log 16) worst-case work in the bounded profile.
algorithm_details.complexity_note: This deterministic fixed-width profile does not claim the classic expected O(log log U) bound of randomized y-fast trie variants.
